title: The organizational design and development technique
blurb: Describe the five steps of the organizational design and development technique and recognize which step an activity belongs to.
question: Partway through a project, the project manager arranges a supplier contract to bring in a missing skill and plans to release the specialists afterwards. Which step of the organizing technique is this?

teach.body: Formally: the organizing practice's technique is organizational design and development, with five steps: understand the organizational ecosystem, design the project ecosystem, develop the project ecosystem, manage ongoing changes to the project ecosystem, and transition the project into the organizational ecosystem. In plain English: learn how the existing organizations work, design the project's temporary set-up, grow it, adjust it as needs change, and hand everything back at the end.

teach.caption: Steps 3 and 4 continue throughout the project; step 5 happens at closure.

rows.label: What
values: The existing organizations: business, users, suppliers
The temporary set-up created for the project

rows.label: Has
values: Its own people, relationships, ways of working

teach.caption: The project ecosystem sits where the business, user and supplier ecosystems overlap.

head: Step
Typical activities
rows: Existing structures, governance, decisions needing business approval, policies
People and resources needed, integrated working practices, behaviours and culture
Onboarding (site visit, induction, certification), skills assessment, succession
New capabilities, people on and off, robust change management
Hand products, people and learning back to the business
teach.caption: Design is shaped by the work breakdown structure and the commercial management approach.

teach.body: Projects unite people from organizations that already have their own structures and governance. If the project ignores them, approvals stall and people are pulled back to their day jobs. If it simply copies them, cross-functional work suffers. The technique makes the project a distinct, temporary entity that still fits its parent organizations, and keeps it fit as the project's needs change.

children.edge: Choosing people and ways of working
children.label: Design

teach.h: Worked scenario: upgrading a rail depot
teach.body: At Glenmoor Rail, project manager Nadia Fraser first maps which depot decisions need the operations board's approval and how staff rotas work (understand). She then decides which engineers and contractors are needed and how they will work together (design). New contractors get a site induction and safety certification (develop). When signalling work starts, she uses the commercial approach to bring in signalling specialists and plans their release (manage ongoing changes). At closure, the depot, its staff and the lessons pass back to operations (transition).

teach.text: Traps: onboarding such as a site visit or induction is DEVELOP, not design. Bringing people on and off the project as capabilities change is MANAGE ONGOING CHANGES, not transition. Transition is the hand-back at closure.

items: Five steps: understand, design, develop, manage ongoing changes, transition.
Understand the existing organizations before designing the project's own set-up.
Develop = onboarding, skills, culture, succession; manage changes = new capabilities, people on and off.
Transition hands products, people and learning back to the business at closure.

summary: You can now name the five steps of the organizational design and development technique, describe what happens in each, and place a given activity in the right step.

A.q: Which is the first step of the organizational design and development technique?
options: Manage ongoing changes to the ecosystem
A.why: The technique starts by understanding the organizational ecosystem, before the project ecosystem is designed (6.3.1).

whyNot.0: Design is the second step; it needs an understanding of the existing organizations first.
whyNot.3: Managing ongoing changes is the fourth step.

A.q: A specialist joining in the third stage is given an induction and a skills assessment. Which step is this?
options: Transition the project to the business
A.why: Develop the project ecosystem includes onboarding people (induction, site visits, certification) and skills assessment.

whyNot.0: Understanding the organizational ecosystem looks at existing structures and governance.
whyNot.1: Design decides the people, resources and working practices needed, not how individuals are inducted.
whyNot.2: Transition hands products, people and learning back at closure.

A.q: Which step hands the project's products, people and learning back to the business?
options: Transition the project into the organizational ecosystem
Manage the ongoing changes to the project ecosystem
Develop the project ecosystem ahead of the next stage
Understand the organizational ecosystem at closure
A.why: The transition step moves products, people and learning back into the organizational ecosystem at closure.

whyNot.1: Managing ongoing changes adjusts the project ecosystem during the project.
whyNot.2: Developing the ecosystem builds the team; it does not hand anything back.
whyNot.3: Understanding the organizational ecosystem is the first step, done at the start.

B.q:
Which two statements about the technique are correct?
1. The design step includes determining the people and resources needed.
2. The transition step happens at the start of initiation.
3. Managing ongoing changes includes moving people onto and off the project.
4. The understand step is carried out after the project closes.
B.why: Design determines the people and resources needed (1); managing ongoing changes transitions people onto and off the project as capabilities change (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: transition happens at closure.
whyNot.1: Both are false: transition is at closure, and understanding comes first.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the understand step comes first, before design.

B.q: Partway through delivery, the project needs a capability it lacks. The PM uses the commercial approach to contract specialists and plans their release later. Which step is this?
options: Transition the project to the business
Manage ongoing changes to the ecosystem
B.why: As capabilities needed change over the lifecycle, the PM ensures the commercial management approach supports this and transitions people onto and off the project.

whyNot.0: Design sets up the project ecosystem at the start; this is a change during delivery.
whyNot.1: Understanding the organizational ecosystem is about existing structures and governance.
whyNot.2: Transition is the hand-back at closure, not releasing specialists mid-project.

options: The existing organizations, each with its own governance
The temporary people and structures set up for the project
The chart of the roles in the project management team
The hierarchy of all the work done during the project
B.why: The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project.

whyNot.0: The existing organizations with their own governance are the organizational ecosystem.
whyNot.2: A chart of roles is the PMT structure.
whyNot.3: The hierarchy of all work is the work breakdown structure.

C.q: Which step looks at which decisions need business approval, and which ecosystem does it examine?
C.why: Understanding the organizational ecosystem covers existing structures, governance and the decisions that need business approval.

whyNot.0: Design organizes work and people for the project; it builds on the understanding gained first.
whyNot.1: The step is right, but it examines the existing organizational ecosystem.
whyNot.2: Transition hands the project back at closure.

C.q: Which step is shaped by the WBS and the commercial management approach, and what does it decide?
options: Design; how to organize work and people
Develop; how to onboard new members
Transition; how to hand back products
C.why: Design concerns how to organize work and people to achieve the project's objectives, shaped by the WBS and commercial management approach.

whyNot.1: Develop covers onboarding, but the step shaped by the WBS and commercial approach is design.
whyNot.2: Transition hands back products at closure.
whyNot.3: Understanding existing governance is the first step.

C.q: Which step requires a robust change management procedure so impacts on the project ecosystem are considered in decisions, and who ensures it?
options: Manage ongoing changes; the project manager
C.why: In managing ongoing changes, the project manager must ensure a robust change management procedure so impacts across the project ecosystem are considered.

whyNot.0: Develop covers onboarding and skills; the change management point belongs to managing ongoing changes.
whyNot.2: The step is right, but the project manager ensures it; assurance checks independently for the board.
whyNot.3: Design is the second step and the business layer sits outside the PMT.

reteach.title: Setting up a pop-up restaurant
reteach.question: A chef opens a six-month pop-up inside a hotel. What must she do from start to finish with the people involved?

blocks.body: She learns how the hotel works: who signs off menus, its staff rules (understand). She plans her kitchen team and how they will work with hotel staff (design). She inducts and trains new cooks (develop). When summer bookings rise, she hires extra staff and lets them go in autumn (manage ongoing changes). When the pop-up ends, equipment, staff and recipes return to the hotel (transition).

blocks.text: Hiring and releasing seasonal staff mid-way is managing ongoing changes; transition is the hand-back at the very end.

explain.body: The organizational ecosystem is the existing organizations with their own structures and governance. The project ecosystem is the temporary set-up created for the project.

options: The temporary set-up created for the project's work
The work packages handed to the team managers
The existing organizations with their own structures
The project board together with its assurance roles
test.why: The organizational ecosystem is the existing organizations (business, users, suppliers) with their own structures, governance and culture.

whyNot.0: The temporary set-up is the project ecosystem.
whyNot.1: Work packages are planning and control products.
whyNot.3: The board and assurance are part of the project management team.

explain.body: First understand existing structures and governance. Then design the project ecosystem: people and resources, integrated working practices, behaviours and culture.

test.q: Determining the people and resources the project needs is part of which step?
options: Transition the project to the business
test.why: Design the project ecosystem includes determining the people and resources needed.

whyNot.1: Develop is about onboarding and growing the team once designed.
whyNot.2: Understanding looks at the existing organizations.
whyNot.3: Transition is the hand-back at closure.

explain.body: Develop: onboarding, skills assessment, culture, succession. Manage ongoing changes: capabilities change over the lifecycle, so people move on and off and change management considers the impacts.

test.q: Succession planning for key team members is part of which step?
options: Transition the project to the business
test.why: Developing the project ecosystem includes onboarding, skills assessment, culture and succession.

whyNot.0: Design sets up the people and working practices; succession is ongoing development.
whyNot.1: Transition hands the project back at closure.
whyNot.2: Understanding looks at the existing organizations.

explain.body: At closure, the project's products, people and learning are handed back into the organizational ecosystem.

test.q: When does the transition step mainly take place?
test.why: Transition hands products, people and learning back to the business at closure.

whyNot.0: Starting up is when the project is being set up, not handed back.
whyNot.3: Before the mandate there is no project to transition.
